neighbours.label: awareness held while acting: ' knowing (that)', 'knowingly', 'in full awareness', 'acutely/fully aware', as against acting while hoping or wishing
fire: The driver kept going through the storm, knowing that the bridge might be closed.
In the end she resigned, knowing full well that nobody would replace her.
Every investor entered the deal fully aware of the risks involved.
The senator spoke in full awareness that her words would be quoted.
Our team is acutely aware that the deadline cannot move again.
The tenants knowingly broke the lease by keeping three dogs.
He smiled at the judge, knowing that the verdict was already decided.
Many parents sign up their children, fully aware that the camp is strict.
quiet: The driver kept going through the storm, hoping that the bridge would be open.
In the end she resigned, wishing that somebody would replace her soon.
Every investor entered the deal eager for the profits involved.
The senator spoke in a loud voice so that her words would be heard.
Our team is very happy that the deadline has moved again.
The tenants happily kept the lease and adopted three dogs.
He smiled at the judge, hoping that the verdict would be kind.
Many parents sign up their children, excited that the camp is fun.

predictions: fire 0.4-0.9 on ' knowing', ' full', ' fully' or 'utely' in an awareness frame; the same sentences with hoping, wishing or eager below 0.2
short: acting with awareness: knowing that, fully aware
